hook: One traversal order turns any binary search tree back into a sorted list. How?

narration.text: This is a binary search tree — every left child is smaller than its parent, every right child is larger.
In-order traversal visits the entire left subtree first, recursively, before touching the node itself.
Once the left side is exhausted, it visits the node, then recurses into the right subtree the same way.
Repeating this at every level, left then node then right, walks the whole tree in one pass.
Seven nodes, one recursive rule — and the visit order comes out perfectly sorted, for free.

youtube.title: In-Order Tree Traversal, Visually
youtube.description: Why an in-order traversal of a binary search tree always visits nodes in sorted order — left subtree, node, right subtree, recursively.
